title: CSV Data Explorer CLI
blurb: A command-line tool that profiles any CSV and writes a cleaning report.
brief: Build a command-line tool that takes a CSV file and prints a profile of it: column types, missing values, duplicates, summary statistics, correlations between numeric columns, and suggested cleaning steps. Then add a --clean option that applies safe fixes and writes a new CSV. This is the first thing you do on every real dataset, so make it solid.
requirements: Accept a CSV path (and an optional --clean output path) through a command-line interface
Report each column's inferred type, missing count and percentage, and number of unique values
Compute summary statistics (mean, std, min, max, quartiles) for numeric columns
Compute pairwise correlations and flag pairs above a threshold
Detect duplicate rows and report them
Apply cleaning: fill or flag missing values, drop duplicates, and report what changed
deliverables: Source code organized into small functions
A README showing example output on a public dataset
Unit tests for at least the missing-value and duplicate logic
stretch: Detect outliers with the IQR rule and report them
Export the profile as Markdown or HTML
resume_bullet: Built a CLI data-profiling tool (Python/pandas) that automates EDA and cleaning for arbitrary CSVs, covered by unit tests.
